patterns.title: Extinction share falls as ambient oxygen rises (FLEX droplet)
patterns.statement: Of tests at 12 % O₂ (8 tests), 100.0 % ended in extinction; at 24 % O₂ (19 tests) the share is 36.8 %. Counts are from the FLEX table, not a fitted model.

patterns.title: Opposed flow spread more slowly than concurrent flow at 20 cm/s
patterns.statement: Published spread rates at 20 cm/s: concurrent 1.8, 2.1 mm/s, opposed 1.3 mm/s. Only 3 records report a rate, so this is a small-sample comparison.

patterns.title: SAFFIRE-III Sample 2: ignition on the edge without spread in 160 s
patterns.statement: Camera S2C2 shows a flame line on the ignition edge from about 61 s; sample thermocouples stayed near 14 °C over the 160 s recorded. Recording ended at 160 s, so later spread is not excluded.

patterns.title: Lunar-gravity records are limited to two LUCI tests
patterns.statement: The loaded catalog holds 2 lunar-gravity records (LUCI). Both are published; neither includes a measured extinction threshold.

findings.title: low flow sensitivity
findings.statement: Microgravity flames were found to be especially sensitive to air flow speed in the range 0 to 5 cm/s.

findings.title: dim blue low flow
findings.statement: At the lowest speeds examined (less than 1 cm/s) all the flames tended to become dim blue and very stable. However, heat loss at these very low convective rates is small so the flames can burn for a long time.

findings.title: flames survive below 1
findings.statement: Flames survived at airflow less than 1 cm/s.

findings.title: sibal quench speeds
findings.statement: The quenching speeds were found to be between 1 and 5 cm/s with higher speed in lower oxygen atmosphere.

findings.title: sibal spread trends
findings.statement: Flames spread more slowly across the narrower samples, at lower flow velocities and at lower O2 percentages.

findings.title: sibal 10 vs 5
findings.statement: Compared with the 10-cm/s case, the 5-cm/s case has a shorter flame and spreads more slowly.

findings.title: sibal 10 duration
findings.statement: The whole combustion process took about 40 s.

findings.title: sibal 5 duration
findings.statement: Because the flow speed is lower, it took more than 60 s to burn the whole sample.

findings.title: pmma rod limits
findings.statement: Both blowoff and quenching limits were obtained at several oxygen concentrations.

findings.title: low g burns lower o2
findings.statement: Previous testing at microgravity and Lunar gravity indicated that some materials burned to lower oxygen concentrations in low gravity than in normal gravity, although the low g extinction limit criteria are not the same as 1g due to time constraints in drop testing.

findings.title: luci first lunar
findings.statement: These are the first-ever, extended-duration (greater than 25 seconds) combustion tests performed in simulated Lunar gravity.

findings.title: luci fm2
findings.statement: Finally, the experiment is a steppingstone to the ultimate goal of performing burn tests on the Lunar surface in the Flammability of Materials on the Moon (FM2) experiment which is planned to launch in late 2026.

findings.title: sibal lunar downward
findings.statement: SIBAL fabric has been found to only burn downward in air in lunar gravity (via Lunar gravity centrifuge and parabolic flight) where on Earth’s gravity it extinguishes immediately after ignition.

findings.title: confinement small gap
findings.statement: For all baffle types, the flame either fails to ignite or extinguishes before reaching the end of the sample when the inter-baffle distance is too small (~ 1 cm). This is attributed to the reduction of oxygen supply to the flame zone and heat loss to the baffles.

findings.title: exploration atmosphere
findings.statement: An “exploration atmosphere” of 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia), 34% O2, 66% N2 has been recommended by NASA for future Moon and Mars missions as a compromise that balances subsequent pre-EVA prebreathe duration, hypoxia, and flammability risk, assuming a 29.6 kPa (4.3 psi) spacesuit.

findings.title: saffire vs bass
findings.statement: While steady flame spread was also observed, the flame spread rates at the steady state in Saffire were significantly lower than those obtained in BASS even at the same oxygen percentage and flow rate. The different spread rates were suspected to be due to the different confined conditions introduced by the large and small flow ducts used in these two experiments.

findings.title: bass duct
findings.statement: The tests were performed in the 250-L free volume Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) in the Destiny Lab of the International Space Station (ISS).

findings.title: bass duct size
findings.statement: The flow duct measured 7.6 by 7.6 by 17 cm with rounded internal corners for smooth laminar flow through the duct.

findings.title: hw duct
findings.statement: The black anodized 7.6- by 7.6- by 17-cm rectangular flow duct with rounded corners was originally built to perform gas jet diffusion flame studies (Ref. 10).

findings.title: hw fan
findings.statement: The flow was blown through the duct using a variable speed fan.

findings.title: hw straightener
findings.statement: The flow then passed through a honeycomb flow straightener and an inlet screen to reduce swirl.

findings.title: hw radiometer
findings.statement: Inside the test section was a nozzle for N2 flow, a movable scale, and an Oriel® 71768 thermopile detector (Newport Corporation) with a CaFl window (spectral range of 0.13 to 11 µm) in the downstream top back corner of the duct viewing the upstream direction.

findings.title: hw still camera
findings.statement: The top window was used by a Nikon D300s 12.3-megapixel digital color still camera with a 60-mm lens that provided 4,320- by 2,968-pixel images.

findings.title: hw video
findings.statement: The video camera had an overlay that displayed the N2 flow rate (cm3/min), fan voltage (10× V), air velocity transducer reading (cm/s), and the radiometer signal.

findings.title: hw igniter
findings.statement: The samples were manually ignited with a Kanthal® A–1 29-gauge hot-wire igniter coil with a nominal hot wire resistance of 0.8 to 1 Ω, powered by 3.5 to 3.8 amps when the astronaut manually pulled the deployment lever to move the igniter into position.

findings.title: hw samples
findings.statement: The flat samples were 1 or 2 cm wide.

findings.title: hw exit
findings.statement: The duct exit contained a perforated copper plate followed by a brass screen to provide heat rejection and a cold surface for soot deposition.

findings.title: hw nitrogen
findings.statement: Working volume of MSG was diluted using ISS N2 gas.

findings.title: saffire first large fire
findings.statement: For the first time, a large-scale fire was intentionally set inside a spacecraft while in orbit.

findings.title: saffire steady wide flame
findings.statement: Unlike 1-g, the results revealed that a steady flame could be achieved even for a wide sample burning in concurrent-flow.

findings.title: saffire nomex not ignited
findings.statement: Despite this significant heating load, the fabric was not ignited.

findings.title: saffire thick fuel pinned
findings.statement: Quote withheld: source copyright may include third-party material.

findings.title: saffire flame jumped gap
findings.statement: Quote withheld: source copyright may include third-party material.

findings.title: saffire alarm 981 s
findings.statement: Quote withheld: source copyright may include third-party material.

findings.title: saffire co co2 limits
findings.statement: Quote withheld: source copyright may include third-party material.

findings.title: saffire practical scale kw
findings.statement: Quote withheld: source copyright may include third-party material.

findings.title: flex loi lower
findings.statement: Observed LOI values for these fuels appear to be slightly lower than initially expected.

findings.title: flex test conditions
findings.statement: The droplets had initial diameters between 2 and 5 mm, and they were burned in oxidizing atmospheres at ambient temperature and various pressures between 0.70 and 3.05 atm, over ranges of dilution of oxygen with nitrogen, with carbon dioxide, and with mixtures thereof.

findings.title: acme spherical flames
findings.statement: The microgravity environment avoids buoyancy-induced flicker and enables the creation of spherical flames, allowing numerical models to focus computational power on transport phenomena and chemical kinetics.

gaps.title: No combustion records at Mars gravity (0.38 g)
gaps.detail: The loaded catalog has no record at 0.38 g. Lunar gravity has two LUCI records, taken from a published paper: NASA's PSI database holds no partial-gravity combustion data yet.

gaps.title: Sample 2 camera 1 is not in the archive
gaps.detail: The DoD table lists S2C2 only. The CSV lists S2C1, so the second Sample 2 view is missing.

gaps.title: SAFFIRE-III sensor positions on the sample are not documented
gaps.detail: Without positions, the sensor that is nearest the flame cannot be identified, and spread speed cannot be converted to distance.

gaps.title: Single run per SAFFIRE-III sample
gaps.detail: Detection latencies and the Sample 2 result come from one run each. Repeatability is not measured.

gaps.title: Opposed-flow records are few
gaps.detail: Only 1 opposed-flow record reports a spread rate at 20 cm/s in the published tables.

gaps.title: Some PSI investigations are still missing
gaps.detail: SAME, SAME-R, ACME (PSI-159), SPICE, CFI and a BASS-II test log are now in the catalog. Still not loaded: CFI-G, BRE, E-FIELD Flames, SLICE, FLEX-2 beyond the CFI tests, DAFT. The BASS-II test log (PSI-25) may repeat some BASS-II records taken from the published summary; they could not be matched test by test.

statements.title: S1
statements.summary: Flame spread across sample; sample thermocouples exceeded 100 C at 66.5 s after 60 s igniter; reached about 1000 C

statements.title: S2
statements.summary: Flame line on ignition edge at about 61 s, did not spread; sample thermocouples stayed near 14 C; radiometers 2 and 4 rose about 10 mW/cm2 until about 140 s

oxygen.title: Ambient oxygen vs. droplet extinction share
oxygen.caption: FLEX droplet tests, binned by initial O₂. Counts from the measured table.

airflow.title: Flow speed vs. spread rate (published)
airflow.caption: Only records that report a spread rate. Concurrent and opposed are shown as separate series.
